scope: ASSETS stage step 1 — search-family planning only. No downloads, no contact sheets, no changes to frozen narration, approved storyboard, Playbook, or renderer contract.

statistics.note: SF-05 (title surface) covers two slots (N002-S1, N032-S2) but requires TWO distinct assets: the storyboard mandates a visual rhyme between opening title and ending — same imagery language, deliberately different clips.

priorityOrder.reason: cold open (N001), money-question object, thresholds, and title/ending visual-rhyme surface (N002-S1 + N032-S2).
major conceptual transitions (time-at-scale, one-way time, the lived-morning pivot) and the competence backbone used across the essay.
highest cliché-risk abstract/list passages (someday list, calendars, inertia, pensive solitude, binary-dissolve).

searchFamilies.name: End-of-day commuter crowd
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Routine human flow at day's end, neither tragic nor triumphant; the film's opening address and 'everyone sells time' normalization.
searchQueries: commuters leaving office evening crowd slow
subway platform crowd end of workday
rush hour pedestrians street level calm
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Avoid zombie-commute framing and ant-swarm aerials (storyboard avoid-list).

searchFamilies.name: Money objects in domestic light
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: The money question made physical and quiet: worn wallet, payslip, coin jar — objects touched, not counted.
searchQueries: wallet keys kitchen table evening natural light
payslip envelope kitchen table natural light
household bills unopened mail table quiet
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Hard avoid: stock charts, cash stacks, calculators, money-pile imagery.

searchFamilies.name: Small daily transactions
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Exchange as the episode's core metaphor: receipts, meters, a hand handing over value — restrained, non-literal.
searchQueries: hand taking receipt counter close up

searchFamilies.name: Thresholds and undecided moments
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Choice withheld: doorway pauses, forked paths, a gate passed daily — small scale, real weight, no answer implied.
searchQueries: open doorway quiet interior adjacent rooms natural light
park gate beside daily walking route observational
side street entrance passed by pedestrians ordinary
unentered path edge of neighborhood calm
searchFamilies.riskNotes: APPROVED WITH REVISION (P0): prefer environments where a choice is perceptible without an actor visibly 'acting undecided'. Avoid doorway-back-view contemplation, fork-in-the-road symbolism, silhouettes, signposts, and other decision clichés.

searchFamilies.name: Title surface — quiet interior with negative space
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Still, softly lit interior composed for the title layer (opening) and its closing rhyme (ending). Same visual language, TWO distinct assets — do not reuse one clip for both.
searchQueries: soft window light empty room interior minimal
cup tea table late afternoon light quiet
calm interior negative space window light
searchFamilies.mediaPreference: video (near-static) or photo with Ken Burns
searchFamilies.riskNotes: APPROVED (P0) with selection note: treat opening/ending as a subtle visual rhyme — N002: a quiet space that feels open/waiting; N032: similar visual grammar with a sense that time has passed. Do not make this symbolism overt. No faces, no busy composition, no on-screen typography in footage, no sunrise-through-window cliché for N032-S2.

searchFamilies.name: Competence shown through action
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: The essay's backbone: skilled hands, quiet expertise, work done well, meaningful work with quiet satisfaction — competence intact even when appetite changes.
searchQueries: professional working focused hands close up
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Avoid stressed-office tropes, thumbs-up teamwork, genius-glow effects, superhero framing.

searchFamilies.name: Mentoring and generativity
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Contribution beyond oneself: teaching, mentoring, caregiving — gentle outward-facing activity without halo lighting.

searchFamilies.name: Accumulated career evidence
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: A life's constructed identity: worn tools, marked notebooks, diplomas, early work beside mature work, a thank-you note still pinned.
searchQueries: worn desk tools years of use detail
home office bookshelf diplomas lived in
workshop early work beside finished work
searchFamilies.riskNotes: No wall-of-fame boast framing, no trash/discarding imagery.

searchFamilies.name: Calm family and domestic life
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: What stability buys: dinners, lamplight, children doing homework, a household running honestly — shelter as a real good.
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Avoid lifestyle-ad gloss, perfect-family advertising, sentimental hugs.

searchFamilies.name: Time at scale — light and seasons over familiar places
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Years passing without calendars: day into dusk over a city, subtle seasonal light on the same street, weather changing over stable land.
searchQueries: residential street dusk windows lit static
same street different light subtle season change
weather moving over calm landscape wide
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Timelapse overuse is a named storyboard risk; avoid dramatic winter-to-summer jumps and apocalyptic skies.

searchFamilies.name: Solitary pause — attention turning inward
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Competence intact, appetite gone; people mid-thought between rooms, at windows, porches, kitchens — no single protagonist by the end.
searchQueries: person looking out window quiet afternoon
person standing between two rooms home light
person sitting alone porch natural light
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Pensive stock stare, rain-on-window, mirror monologue, answer-in-eyes close-up are all on the avoid list.

searchFamilies.name: Youth in open motion
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: The building years, the assumed future, and the body still fully in use: studying, commuting, hiking, swimming — vitality framed as finite and present, no countdown.
searchQueries: young adults commuting city morning motion

searchFamilies.name: Ordinary mornings
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: One lived morning instead of a list: alarm, coffee, coat, door — and later, waking without an alarm, sunlight crossing a table.
searchQueries: waking without alarm stretching morning light
sunlight moving across table empty house
searchFamilies.riskNotes: List-shaped narration (N011); keep as one lived morning, not one image per line.

searchFamilies.name: Neutral routine and the work-shaped day
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Duty shown neutrally: same commute, same entrance, coming home in the dark, an unremarkable workday by design.
searchQueries: coming home evening coat dark hallway
ordinary workday desk neutral nothing happens
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Avoid collapse-on-couch, alcohol tropes, quit-your-boss meme energy.

searchFamilies.name: Holding on — sunk-cost gestures
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Persistence caught in small gestures: late-night desk light, a grip tightening on a rail, the same papers rearranged.
searchQueries: late night desk lamp working alone

searchFamilies.name: Financial duties, humane register
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Security is real: mortgage letter on the kitchen table, school bags by the door, groceries, payday rhythms.
searchFamilies.riskNotes: No debt-horror framing, no countdown motifs.

searchFamilies.name: Shelter and weather
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Protection valued without illusion: a home steady in bad weather seen through a window; a safe-looking house at night that is clearly not permanent.
searchQueries: rain on window cozy interior view out
house exterior night warm windows quiet

searchFamilies.name: Small creation — hands for their own sake
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Non-career meaning: bread rising, a half-built birdhouse, pottery, an old radio taken apart — absorbing, impractical, unmonetized.

searchFamilies.name: Unstaged togetherness
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Presence over sentiment: sharing food, walking side by side, late-summer garden with children a little older, ordinary acts with aging parents.
searchQueries: family garden late summer children playing quiet
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Perfect-family advertising, growing-up montage, hospital/deathbed framing all on the avoid list.

searchFamilies.name: Calendars and crowded weeks
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Claims crowding one life; a new calendar with the same handwriting — restrained, observational.
searchQueries: wall calendar new year replacing quiet
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Calendar/planner runs are a named storyboard cliché risk; avoid tear-off pages, color-coded productivity porn.

searchFamilies.name: Work continuing in the background
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: The office running as always; a genuinely pleasant workplace seen tenderly; mild frustration kept beside the point.
searchQueries: office normal day workers background calm

searchFamilies.name: Unused spaces and half-made things
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Traces of imagination treated kindly: an unused instrument, unbought tickets, a garden rarely entered, after-hours emptiness.

searchFamilies.name: Comfortable inertia — someday
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Postponement as the default: plans passing by in one evening, a comfortable chair, wasted-looking time warmly framed.
searchQueries: person sofa evening doing nothing home

searchFamilies.name: Quiet time markers
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Years passing quietly: a child's bicycle grown too small, a height marked on a doorframe — visibility, not dread.

searchFamilies.name: Small autonomy — the lighter schedule
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: The middle answers: leaving in daylight, a self-determined Tuesday, a mixed life, being able to say no to something small.
searchQueries: home workshop laptop mixed use room
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Avoid part-time-idyll fantasy, perfect-balance lifestyle ad, financial-independence number flex.

searchFamilies.name: Planned pause — sabbatical preparation
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: A pause made visible gently: a bag packed weeks ahead, a ticket booked calmly, a chart on a kitchen wall.
searchFamilies.riskNotes: No gap-year cliché, no freedom-numbers montage.

searchFamilies.name: Protected boundary evening
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: An evening explicitly protected: phone face-down, home-office door closed, dinner happening anyway.
searchFamilies.riskNotes: No digital-detox sermon, no burning-phone imagery.

searchFamilies.name: The wide middle between extremes
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Two extremes seen small with a wide, detailed, ordinary middle ground — the binary dissolving spatially.
searchQueries: wide landscape small buildings middle ground depth
town aerial wide ordinary middle distance
long road quiet town middle ground
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Hardest abstract shot; no split-screen gimmick, no binary signposts, no yin-yang symbolism.

searchFamilies.name: One-way time — water and finitude
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Time's arrow stated by landscape, not clocks: water flowing one way past a fixed point, a tide going out, bread cooling.
searchQueries: river flowing past fixed point steady
searchFamilies.riskNotes: N028–N030 cliché alert: absolutely no hourglass, sand running out, melting candles, or reverse playback.

searchFamilies.name: Closing a chapter without ceremony
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Finishing and tidying without drama; a full day ending with its cost and yield both visible in an ordinary evening.
searchQueries: tidying desk finishing project calm evening
quiet evening window day ending ordinary
searchFamilies.riskNotes: No funeral-for-a-career framing, no last-day montage, no ledger imagery.

searchFamilies.name: Social identity — the rehearsed answer
searchFamilies.editorialIntent: Everyday introductions where work is the answer everyone gives — the script rehearsed for years.
searchFamilies.riskNotes: Avoid awkward-party comedy and cringe acting.

uniqueSourcingNotes: N002-S1 and N032-S2 share SF-05 imagery language but MUST be two different assets (storyboard-mandated visual rhyme).
No slot may reuse another slot's downloaded asset silently (series visualRules; storyboard editorialPrinciples).
Provenance (sourceUrl, creator, license, downloadedAt, originalFilename) required for every downloaded asset in inbox/ESSY-0003/visuals.json at manifest time.

workflowLessons.lesson: Search family -> initial candidate batch -> coverage check -> targeted supplemental search when needed.
workflowLessons.detail: A search family reduces duplicated retrieval work; it does not imply that one fixed candidate batch must cover every slot. Observed on ESSY-0003 P0 pass: SF-01 and SF-05 were fully covered by the initial batch; SF-02 and SF-04 required targeted supplemental searches with revised briefs.
workflowLessons.disposition: Retrospective consideration only; Playbook intentionally NOT modified yet.

workflowLessons.lesson: Candidate validation must evaluate returned asset semantics, not only whether it was returned for an approved query. Query match != editorial match.
workflowLessons.detail: Slug/title/description and visual preview can reveal retrieval false positives. Observed on ESSY-0003 P0: SF-01 photo fallback 'silhouetted commuters at sunset' passed the approved query but violated the silhouette cliche ban; SF-04 initial batch returned real-estate-style interiors for doorway queries.
workflowLessons.disposition: Retrospective consideration only; Playbook intentionally NOT modified yet.

workflowLessons.lesson: Asset uniqueness is subordinate to editorial coherence.
workflowLessons.detail: Non-adjacent intentional reuse may be preferable to inserting a weaker stock asset, provided reuse is explicitly recorded and later checked in sequence QA. Observed on ESSY-0003 P0: pexels-video-6279418 deliberately reused for N001-S3 and N019-S1 as a recurring lived-in-threshold motif (provenance entries marked intentionalMotifReuse; sequence-QA check required).
workflowLessons.disposition: Retrospective consideration only; Playbook intentionally NOT modified yet.

workflowLessons.lesson: Search-family batching needs a semantic-diversity / coverage check when one family spans many slots. A family can be conceptually coherent while still requiring multiple visual sub-modes. Candidate count alone is not coverage.
workflowLessons.detail: Observed on ESSY-0003 P1: SF-10's initial batch skewed entirely to residential-street dusk (one temporal mechanism for eight slots spanning day-dusk, seasons, weather, and inhabited/quiet shifts); SF-06's initial batch skewed to craft/workshop imagery, which would visually redefine 'competence' as craftsmanship alone. Both required targeted supplemental passes with mechanism-diverse briefs. Also applied positively: SF-29's three slots deliberately vary the one-way-time metaphor (river -> tide -> bread cooling) instead of collapsing into water imagery.
workflowLessons.disposition: Retrospective consideration only; Playbook intentionally NOT modified yet.

nextStepAfterApproval: Batched asset search per family (P0 first), candidate review, then selection and inbox/ESSY-0003 handoff.
